source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, LRO LOLA EXTRAS/ILLUMINATION release 201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011)

avgvisib_85s_060m_201608.DESCRIPTION: This data product is a map of the average illumination by the solar disc of the Lunar South Pole at a resolution of 60 m/pix by 60 m/pix, true at the pole in polar stereographic (spherical) projection. The calculations are based on the LOLA elevation map LDEM_85S_060M and are described in [MAZARICOETAL2011]. The values are continuous between 0 (permanent shadow) and 1, and indicate the percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc). Note a scaling was applied to fit the data in the INT16 value range. This label describes an IMG file in the form of a binary resampling with pixel registration.

lpsr_85s_060m_201608.DESCRIPTION: This data product is a map of the permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) in the lunar South Pole. The map resolution is 60m/pix by 60m/pix, true at the pole in polar stereographic (spherical) projection. Calculations are based on LOLA topographic data and are described in [MAZARICOETAL2011]. The values are binary, indicating whether a pixel is in permanent shadow (1) or not (0). Note a scaling was applied. This label describes an IMG file in the form of a binary resampling with pixel registration.
